html:
SMTO-SSH-0009 — SMTO hasn't verified that remote computer for sudo yet

GUID: f549bbfe-60f6-53ac-9fa7-88f73fcb9f67
Slug: remote-privilege-target-unverified
Domain: SSH · Subsystem: remote

What happened

  • Before running a command with sudo on another computer over SSH, SMTO must already have checked that exact computer and account in this conversation. It hadn't, so it refused. Nothing was run on the remote computer or on the Gateway.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In this same conversation, ask the Agent to run a simple command on that computer over SSH without sudo, for example: ssh user@host hostname. That first ordinary connection lets SMTO check and remember the computer and account.
  2. If you've connected to that computer with more than one account, include the account name in the address, such as admin@server1. SMTO won't guess which of several accounts should get administrator rights.
  3. Ask for the sudo command as one plain SSH command with sudo inside the quotes, such as ssh admin@server1 'sudo systemctl status nginx'. SMTO only allows remote sudo through a single, direct SSH command, not one chained to other SSH commands.

What success looks like

  • The Agent runs the sudo command on the remote computer and shows its result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or that computer. Don't wrap the SSH command in sudo on the Gateway instead; that would run on the wrong computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Remote elevation was refused before dispatch: the command could not be bound to exactly one verified SSH host/port/account/host-key/config identity in this working context, was not a single literal ssh invocation, or contained nested remote (ssh/sshpass) intent.

What this means

  • Remote privilege planning cannot bind one literal SSH command to one matching pinned target/account, detects nested remote intent, or emits the explicit unsupported-target refusal. Continuity evidence and command outcome are separate. Only the explicit pre-dispatch privilege refusal proves no new execution; observation failure alone cannot prove that a prior SSH command had no effect.

Why this can happen

  • Remote privilege planning cannot bind one literal SSH command to one matching pinned target/account, detects nested remote intent, or emits the explicit unsupported-target refusal.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact SSH argv, retained account/fingerprint and target ownership; inspect executed:false on the refusal.

How to fix it

  • Establish the SSH identity first with an ordinary verified SSH operation in the same conversation (for example ssh user@host hostname), then send the elevated command as a single literal ssh invocation with sudo inside the remote command (ssh user@host 'sudo id'). Specify the user explicitly when several verified accounts match the host, and do not nest ssh or sshpass in the remote command.
  • Inspect and verify the selected SSH target and pinned identity before requesting remote elevation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported verified target is established before exact remote elevation is requested.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Continuity evidence and command outcome are separate. Only the explicit pre-dispatch privilege refusal proves no new execution; observation failure alone cannot prove that a prior SSH command had no effect.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
